justification: The GHOST faithfully reconstructs the ORIGINAL's core semantic structure and all material claims. ORIGINAL: (1) companion law of self-similarity states the whole's good is paramount; (2) this law has a seam—whoever defines the whole defines the good; (3) a second co-equal law corrects this: no node alone adjudicates the boundary; (4) the whole is checked from outside; (5) this law keeps the first from becoming a license; (6) it is ratified, not provisional. GHOST restates: (1) the whole-serving principle has a flaw—the definer of 'whole' controls 'good'; (2) a partner principle of equal standing corrects it: no single part settles the boundary alone; (3) the call comes from beyond the part; (4) nothing judges its own scope; (5) without this companion the first becomes a permission slip; (6) this law is settled, not open. The logical structure is preserved: flaw → fix, co-equality, external validation, permanence. The GHOST uses paraphrase ('seam' → 'flaw', 'checked from outside' → 'call comes from beyond') but preserves all relations and claims. No material content is lost or invented. The GHOST is structured (coherent boundary principle with external validation) and demonstrates recursion (the companion law refines but does not contradict the first, allowing iterative refinement of both).
